text:
alex_support: VoltHealth reporting sudden 429 flood exactly at top-of-hour after our 22:00 deploy. customer sees `Too Many Requests` across many clients. attaching a short log sample.

volthealth_ops: yep, looks like a fanout when devices wake up on schedule. we have ~15k devices reconnecting every hour. we only started seeing this after the deploy but it might be coincidental.

alex_support: thanks. log snippet shows rate headers: `x-ratelimit-limit-minute: 1200`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-minute: 0`, `x-ratelimit-reset: 1715010000` — large number of parallel streams all emptied the minute window.

maya_se: can you paste the client pattern? are devices using exponential backoff or hammering in parallel? any HTTP/2 multiplexing?

volthealth_ops: they do an immediate batch sync on reconnect (10 parallel requests per device). using our Node gateway with http2 multiplexing enabled. we saw concurrent streams spike to ~40k.

eli_oncall: probable stampede on refill + minute boundary alignment. two quick mitigations: 1) ask customer to jitter reconnects (randomize within 60s), 2) reduce parallelism/streams per client temporarily. also we can route them to a compatible lower-tier model variant as emergency fallback.

ryan_eng: infra note — our minute-based quota + token bucket smoothing isn't visible to clients. recommend enabling per-second smoothing on our gateway for this tenant and enable soft-burst TTL. i can flip a config but need ops approval.

infra-bot: INCIDENT-TRIAGE created (#INC-6542) — assigned to ryan_eng and eli_oncall. current quota window shows sustained 1m saturation at 22:00 UTC.

alex_support: quick repro command for the customer to test client-side smoothing:
```
# simple curl loop with jitter
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  sleep $(python -c "import random; print(random.random()*1)")
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"ping"}' &
done
wait
```

maya_se: also send them this recommended client backoff snippet (Node):
```
async function sendWithBackoff(req) {
  for (let i=0;i<5;i++) {
    try { return await axios(req); }
    catch (e) {
      if (e.response && e.response.status===429) {
        await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, Math.pow(2,i)*100 + Math.random()*200));
        continue;
      }
      throw e;
    }
  }
}
```

volthealth_ops: implementing jitter now. any short-term config you can change on our tenant to reduce failures while we roll client patch?

ryan_eng: yes — we can temporarily: 1) enable per-second smoothing for tenant, 2) increase minute quota by 20% for one hour, 3) enable fallback routing to smaller model. i'll coordinate with infra.

eli_oncall: for postmortem please capture: exact device reconnect spread, http2 concurrent_streams, whether token refresh endpoint caused synchronous refreshes, and SDK versions. this will tell us if it's client behavior or an unintended effect from deploy.

alex_support: volthealth, can you share SDK version and whether reconnect uses new auth refresh path?

volthealth_ops: SDK v2.4.1. auth refresh calls token endpoint then does immediate sync; looks like refresh callback triggers the batch. we'll push jitter in 10m and report back.

ryan_eng: noted. i'll apply temporary tenant smoothing now and raise quota for the next hour. will post when done.

infra-bot: CONFIG-CHANGE: per-second-smoothing=on for tenant volthealth (applied) at 1715010200. quota bump +20% applied until 1715013800.

volthealth_ops: saw immediate improvement — 429s dropped by ~85% in the next minute. thanks.

alex_support: great. follow-up actions: client-side jitter + limited parallelism, SDK patch to stagger token refresh, and a postmortem runbook note to consider per-tenant smoothing during scheduled mass reconnects.

eli_oncall: closing triage once postmortem doc is attached to INCIDENT-TRIAGE #INC-6542.

volthealth_ops: will upload postmortem and SDK PR link once done. thanks all :thumbsup:
